# Five-source intake — September 14, 2026

Scope: five supplied originals, 150 PDF pages, in ordered batches B1 (memo and ROD), B2 (supplemental RI), B3 (index and fact sheet). Extraction and rendering do not by themselves count as review. Document publication remains separate from strict verification.

## B1 — action memorandum, EPA 209480 (2 pages)

Both pages read in order using native text, full-page images and Windows OCR. Native OCR misreads 1982/1981 as 1932/1931; images confirm December 30, 1982 and May 1981. Page 1 is a request for RI/FS and anticipated MDNR cooperative agreement, not executed approval. It names William N. Hedeman Jr. and Lee M. Thomas; the attached Enforcement Release is NOT in the supplied two-page file. Reports operation 1971–1981, sandy flat setting, one-quarter mile southwest of municipal well field, and a child's chemical burns after abandonment.

Page 2 requests RI $300,000/40 weeks and FS $150,000/10 weeks, total $450,000 with proposed 100% EPA funding. Immediate removal is being considered, including sewer disconnection and possible slab/soil decontamination. Final cooperative agreement anticipated June 17, 1983. Typed footer is 5-31-83. Approve, Disapprove and Date lines are blank. Handwritten routing annotations include legible June 1983 dates, but some initials/names remain unreadable; they are not substituted for signed authorization. Catalog date should be 1983 with May 31 explicitly described as preparation/footer date, not approval. Lead: executed CA, Enforcement Release and actual funds/implementation record. Later OSC report 209451 describes July 5–August 3, 1983 removal and is a separate record of actual work.

## B1 — signed ROD, EPA 209538 (24 supplied pages)

All 24 native-text pages and four six-page contact sheets inspected in order; fresh Windows OCR applied throughout. Full-size detail checks: pp. 5, 9, 11, 12, 15, 21, 24. Original is 24 PDF pages although technical-data p. 2 states 21 pages. Referenced FFS and original City written comments are not supplied separately; the responsiveness summary IS present on p. 24.

Page coverage:

- 6: site description, three sand aquifers/two clay units, 300-ft municipal aquifer with limited knowledge, 1,500-ft northeast well field; shallow northeast flow, intermediate northwest flow, upper aquifers merge north; historical interpretation. 1971–1978 sewer discharge/exfiltration/drywell; ownership text reads R.H. Meyer while p. 13 enforcement reads R.W. Meyer—preserve discrepancy.

## B2 — supplemental remedial investigation, EPA 209637 (118 supplied pages)

All 118 supplied pages were read in order using native text and rendered pages, with Windows OCR throughout. Narrative contact sheets were followed by full-resolution checks of the maps, tables, logs and material readings. Rotation derivatives were used for landscape maps/tables. The January 1987 issue date is on the title pages; November 1985–April 1986 describes investigation work, not publication. The footer 2.86.88 is not treated as a date. This is historical chromium/cadmium/VOC groundwater evidence, NOT PFAS sampling or proof of a modern Wexford-to-Plett route.

## B3 — Wexford County landfill fact sheet, EPA 421579 (4 pages)

All4 pages read top-to-bottom, columns/tables/maps included, native OCR checked against full images and fresh Windows OCR. Exact SHA match to canonical027-b6b5e1c0bddb; preserve one original and both filename aliases. **Issue is July2006**, while prior name06-20-2006 refers to RI/FS submission dates inside; correct display, retain provenance.

- Page1: County community update, impacts detected north since late1980s, latest investigation since2003. Draft RI and draft FS submittedJune20,2006; monthly MDEQ meetings since previous summer; two-month review with more data collection expected. RI/FS/RAP are distinct steps. FS is not final remedy decision; future RAP requires review/approval. EPA barcode421579, not native OCR421679.
- Page2: three local units, upper sand/gravel contaminated, estimated north-northwest groundwater280–360ft/year; residential wells mostly upper. Intermediate clay stated4 to over30ft, continuous across this investigation area and100,000times less permeable. Lower sand/gravel greater190ft,6 residential wells, no site contaminants reported detected but limited investigation and more planned. West plume attributed to landfill, multiple VOCs declining since2003, highest organics~1200ft north. East plume TCE only organic, unknown source east, highest~3000ft north; Fe/Mn in both. Two plumes extend to upper-aquifer base; lower under-landfill concentrations than north. Primary current-impact/secondary potential-migration zones. Cross-section north arrow, MSL elevation scale, well-replacement screens reviewed. This is Wexford landfill geology, NOT proof its clay unit is the same as Northernaire's or that the two sites share a connected plume.
- Page3: alternatives and entire rating/cost matrix read. Continued interim action$1.3M; point-source treatment$2.5M; deep-well replacement$1.3M; public supply$3.5M, all estimates. Overall medium/medium/medium-high/medium. Public supply high overall protection/state acceptance but low implementability. Community acceptance medium-low for all. Deep-well plan includes shallow abandonment/annual sampling; not approval or implementation evidence. Map shows north arrow, east/west plumes and primary/secondary zones; no invented coordinates.
- Page4: County reports~40 additional residential wells sampled since2004 with changing quarterly network. Wells south/east/west and along41½Road were excluded based on its interpreted flow path; not proof present-day safety. Bottled water/carbon filtration temporary. Five original wells replaced with deeper wells and retained in sampling. Waste relocation initiated2005, three phases, expected >1.8million cubic yards from unlined to lined cells—forecast, not completed tonnage or shipment to Cadillac. Groundwater system reportedly operated since1994, pumps up to750,000gal/day to onsite aeration pond and returns water to aquifer. This is groundwater treatment, NOT WWTP-delivered leachate volume. Planned August3 meeting7pm, tentativeSeptember18 meeting,October10 draftRAP submission; no evidence those later events occurred in this file. John Divozzo, County DPW Director contact. Addressed return postcard referenced but not attached; no new substantive finding depends on it.

The six B3 supplied pages are legible. Index-listed originals and full landfill RI/FS/RAP are separate open leads, not silently marked received or reviewed. Supported findings verified to the supplied fact sheet only; no fresh independent confirmation of its historical estimates or present-day conditions.
